name: Joab
description: David's compatriot living at the time of United Monarchy

points: David asked Ahimelech the Hittite and Abishai the son of Zeruiah, the brother of Joab, Who will go down with me to Saul to the camp? and Abishai said, I will go down with thee; and they came to the people by night, and all lay sleeping.

note.label: 1 Samuel 26: David Spares Saul a Second Time

points: Abner and the servants of Ishbosheth met Joab and the servants of David at the pool of Gibeon, sitting on opposite sides. Abner said, Let the young men arise and play, meaning let them compete and battle one another; the Lord is a man of war, and such contests were done in that day.

note.label: 2 Samuel 2: David Anointed King Over Judah

points: Asahel, one of the three sons of Zeruiah, was as light of foot as a wild roe, meaning he was fast, and he pursued Abner and would not turn aside. Abner warned him again and again to turn off and take another man's armor, not wanting to have to kill him and face Joab his brother.

note.label: 2 Samuel 2: David Anointed King Over Judah

points: Abner called to Joab, asking whether the sword should devour forever, and warned that it would be bitterness in the latter end; he asked how long before Joab bade the people return from following their brethren. Joab answered that unless Abner had spoken, the people would have gone up in the morning, and he blew the trumpet and the people stood still and fought no more.

note.label: 2 Samuel 2: David Anointed King Over Judah

points: Joab returned from pursuing a troop and heard that Abner had come and been sent away in peace. Joab came to the king and said Abner had come to deceive him and to know his going out and coming in; he did not trust Abner, and there was already blood between them, for Abner had killed Asahel his brother.

note.label: 2 Samuel 3: The House of David Waxes Stronger

points: Joab, without David's knowledge, sent messengers after Abner and brought him back to Hebron, took him aside in the gate to speak quietly, and smote him there under the fifth rib, that he died, for the blood of Asahel his brother.
It was payback; Joab's blood was burning for revenge. Abner was unwise to return to that place, knowing what Joab would do, but it was of the Lord.

note.label: 2 Samuel 3: The House of David Waxes Stronger

points: When David heard it, he declared himself and his kingdom guiltless before the Lord forever from the blood of Abner, and laid it on the head of Joab and all his father's house. He commanded Joab and all the people to rend their clothes and gird with sackcloth and mourn before Abner, and the king himself followed the coffin.

note.label: 2 Samuel 3: The House of David Waxes Stronger

points: When David heard it he sent Joab and all the host of the mighty men. The children of Ammon put the battle in array at the gate, and the Syrians were by themselves in the field. Seeing the battle set against him before and behind, Joab chose of the choice men of Israel against the Syrians and delivered the rest into the hand of Abishai his brother against the children of Ammon, each ready to help the other if too strong.

This is how much of a warrior nation Israel is: Joab put his troops in a battle array to fight two enemies at one time. That warrior mentality is already etched inside us; we just have to keep the commandments so it can come back out, as it is going to according to Joel 2.

note.label: 2 Samuel 10: The Children of Ammon and the Syrians Smitten

points: Joab charged them to be of good courage and play the men for their people and the cities of their God. When Joab and his men drew nigh, the Syrians fled before him, and when the children of Ammon saw the Syrians flee, they also fled before Abishai and entered into the city, and Joab returned to Jerusalem.

note.label: 2 Samuel 10: The Children of Ammon and the Syrians Smitten

points: After the year was expired, at the time when kings go forth to battle, David sent Joab and all Israel to destroy the children of Ammon and besiege Rabbah, but David tarried still at Jerusalem. In the evening he walked upon the roof, saw a woman washing herself who was very beautiful, inquired and learned she was Bathsheba the wife of Uriah the Hittite, sent and took her, and lay with her; and she conceived and told David, I am with child.

note.label: 2 Samuel 11: David, Bathsheba, and the Murder of Uriah

points: Uriah told David that the ark and Israel and Judah abode in tents, and Joab and the servants of his lord were encamped in the open fields; so how could he go into his house to eat, drink, and lie with his wife? As David lived, he would not do this thing. David kept him another day and made him drunk, but that evening Uriah still went out to lie on his bed with the servants of his lord and went not down to his house.

note.label: 2 Samuel 11: David, Bathsheba, and the Murder of Uriah

points: In the morning David wrote a letter to Joab and sent it by the hand of Uriah, ordering that Uriah be set in the forefront of the hottest battle and then abandoned, that he might be smitten and die. Joab assigned Uriah to a place where he knew valiant men were, and when the men of the city fought, some of David's servants fell, and Uriah the Hittite died also.

note.label: 2 Samuel 11: David, Bathsheba, and the Murder of Uriah

points: Joab sent and told David all concerning the war, charging the messenger that if the king's wrath arose over drawing so nigh the city, he should then say that Uriah the Hittite was dead also. When the messenger delivered it, David told him to say to Joab, Let not this thing displease thee, for the sword devoureth one as well as another; make the battle stronger and overthrow the city.

note.label: 2 Samuel 11: David, Bathsheba, and the Murder of Uriah

points: Joab the son of Zeruiah perceived that the king's heart was toward Absalom, and sent to Tekoah and fetched a wise woman, telling her to feign herself a mourner, put on mourning apparel, and speak to the king in the manner he taught her.

note.label: 2 Samuel 14: Joab Brings Absalom Home

points: Joab put the words in her mouth. He set up the whole scene to move the king toward bringing Absalom home.

note.label: 2 Samuel 14: Joab Brings Absalom Home

points: The king asked the woman not to hide the thing he would ask: was not the hand of Joab with her in all this? She answered that none could turn to the right hand or the left from what the king had spoken; his servant Joab bade her, and put all these words in her mouth. Joab did this to fetch about this form of speech, and the king was wise, according to the wisdom of an angel of God.

note.label: 2 Samuel 14: Joab Brings Absalom Home

points: David knew. As anointed and worthy as David was, and as wise, there was no way he did not know what kind of man his own right-hand man Joab was. Though David made a mistake, the wisdom never departed from him; David was always on point. This also answers those who use David's mistake to justify their sins; they do not know the Bible, for his house had incest, murder, and now this scheme, and David still saw through all of it.

note.label: 2 Samuel 14: Joab Brings Absalom Home

points: The king told Joab he had done this thing, and commanded him to go bring the young man Absalom again. Joab fell on his face, thanked the king, and said he now knew he had found grace in the king's sight. Joab went to Geshur and brought Absalom to Jerusalem, but the king said, Let him turn to his own house and not see my face.

note.label: 2 Samuel 14: Joab Brings Absalom Home

points: Absalom was trying to get the king's attention, and when Joab would not respond, he set the man's field on fire to force the matter. This was straight craziness, but it finally brought him before the king, and David kissed him.

note.label: 2 Samuel 14: Joab Brings Absalom Home

points: Absalom dwelt two full years in Jerusalem and saw not the king's face. He sent for Joab twice to send him to the king, but Joab would not come, so Absalom had his servants set Joab's barley field on fire. Then Joab came, and Absalom said, Let me see the king's face, and if there be any iniquity in me, let him kill me. Joab told the king, and Absalom came and bowed himself, and the king kissed Absalom.

note.label: 2 Samuel 14: Joab Brings Absalom Home

points: David numbered the people and set captains of thousands and hundreds, sending a third part under Joab, a third under Abishai, and a third under Ittai the Gittite. He said he would surely go forth with them himself.

note.label: 2 Samuel 18: Deal Gently With the Young Man

points: David charged Joab, Abishai, and Ittai to deal gently for his sake with the young man, even with Absalom, and all the people heard the charge. Even after Absalom defiled his concubines and stole the people's hearts, David still sought to make amends with his son.

note.label: 2 Samuel 18: Deal Gently With the Young Man

points: A man told Joab he had seen Absalom hanged in an oak. Joab asked why he had not smitten him to the ground for a reward of ten shekels and a girdle, but the man refused, saying he would not put forth his hand against the king's son for a thousand shekels, because he had heard the king charge them to beware that none touch the young man.

note.label: 2 Samuel 18: Deal Gently With the Young Man

points: The man told Joab that to have killed Absalom would have been to work falsehood against his own life, for nothing is hid from the king, and Joab himself would have set himself against him. Joab said he would not tarry, took three darts, and thrust them through the heart of Absalom while he was yet alive in the midst of the oak.

note.label: 2 Samuel 18: Deal Gently With the Young Man

points: Joab was an evil man with the spirit of murder; he could have brought Absalom back alive for his father to make amends, but he did what he wanted. Ten young men that bore Joab's armor compassed Absalom and smote him and slew him, for a beast will consort to his own like.

note.label: 2 Samuel 18: Deal Gently With the Young Man

points: Joab came into the house and told David he had shamed the faces of all his servants who had saved his life and the lives of his sons, daughters, wives, and concubines, because he loved his enemies and hated his friends. Joab said if Absalom had lived and all of them had died, it would have pleased David well. No one else could speak to the king this way, but Joab knew David's skeletons.

note.label: 2 Samuel 19: The King Returns to His House

points: At the great stone in Gibeon, Joab came to Amasa with a sword secretly fastened, took him by the beard with his right hand as if to kiss him, and smote him in the fifth rib so that his bowels shed to the ground, and he died at one stroke. Joab was grimy and shady, murdering the man who had been named captain in his place.

note.label: 2 Samuel 20: The Revolt of Sheba

points: Joab pursued Sheba through all the tribes to Abel of Beth-maachah, and they cast up a bank against the city and battered the wall to throw it down.

note.label: 2 Samuel 20: The Revolt of Sheba

points: A wise woman of the city called out to Joab, reminding him of the old saying that men would surely ask counsel at Abel, and asked why he would swallow up a city that was a mother in Israel and the inheritance of the Lord. Joab answered that he did not seek to destroy, but only wanted Sheba the son of Bichri, who had lifted up his hand against the king; deliver him and he would depart.

note.label: 2 Samuel 20: The Revolt of Sheba

points: The woman promised that Sheba's head would be thrown over the wall. She went to all the people in her wisdom, and they cut off Sheba's head and cast it out to Joab, who blew the trumpet and retired from the city, every man to his tent, and returned to Jerusalem unto the king.

note.label: 2 Samuel 20: The Revolt of Sheba

points: Joab was over all the host of Israel, and Benaiah the son of Jehoiada over the Cherethites and the Pelethites. Adoram was over the tribute, Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud was recorder, and Sheva was scribe.

note.label: 2 Samuel 20: The Revolt of Sheba

points: The rest of the thirty are named: Asahel the brother of Joab, Elhanan of Bethlehem, and the others down to Uriah the Hittite, thirty and seven in all. Some carry names like Zelek the Ammonite and Uriah the Hittite, but this does not mean they were Hamites in David's army; it means they dwelt in those lands after Israel removed the nations from the coasts.

note.label: 2 Samuel 23: The Last Words of David and His Mighty Men

points: Notwithstanding, the king's word prevailed against Joab and the captains, and they went out to number the people. Joab did not understand that behind it all, verse one, the anger of the Lord was kindled against Israel; it was of the Most High that this happened.

note.label: 2 Samuel 24: David Numbers Israel and Buys the Threshing Floor

points: Joab gave the sum to the king: there were in Israel eight hundred thousand valiant men that drew the sword, and the men of Judah were five hundred thousand men. This did not count the women and the children.

note.label: 2 Samuel 24: David Numbers Israel and Buys the Threshing Floor

points: The blood returns upon Joab's own head and upon his seed, while upon David and his seed and throne there shall be peace forever from the Lord. Benaiah is set over the host in his place.

note.label: 1 Kings 2: The Charge to Solomon and the Kingdom Established

points: The Most High stirred up an adversary to Solomon, Hadad the Edomite, of the king's seed in Edom, for when David was in Edom, Joab remained six months until he had cut off every male, and Hadad fled as a child to Egypt where Pharaoh gave him favor, a house, and a wife.

note.label: 1 Kings 11: Solomon's Strange Wives and the Kingdom Torn

points: Esau was always the first hater and enemy of Israel, comforting himself in the thought of killing us. When Hadad heard David and Joab were dead, he sought to return to his own country.

note.label: 1 Kings 11: Solomon's Strange Wives and the Kingdom Torn

points: The sons of Zeruiah, Abishai, Joab, and Asahel, are named, and Amasa the son of Abigail, whose father was Jether the Ishmaelite.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 2: The Sons of Israel and the Line of Judah

points: David said whoever smote the Jebusites first would be chief and captain. Joab the son of Zeruiah went up first and became chief.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 11: David Anointed and His Mighty Men

points: David dwelt in the castle and built the city round about from Millo, Joab repaired the rest, and David grew greater and greater because the Most High of hosts was with him.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 11: David Anointed and His Mighty Men

points: Abishai the brother of Joab was chief of the second three, and lifted his spear against three hundred and slew them, gaining a name among the three.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 11: David Anointed and His Mighty Men

points: The roll of the valiant men of the armies follows, including Asahel the brother of Joab, Elhanan of Bethlehem, and many more named men from across the tribes.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 11: David Anointed and His Mighty Men

points: The list of his officers follows: Joab over the host, Jehoshaphat the recorder, Zadok and Abimelech the priests, Shavsha the scribe, and Benaiah over the Cherethites and Pelethites.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 18: The Victories of King David

points: Joab found the battle set against him before and behind, so he divided the army: he took the choice of Israel against the Syrians and gave the rest to his brother Abishai against Ammon.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 19: War With Ammon and Syria

points: The Syrians fled before Joab, and when Ammon saw the Syrians flee they also fled into the city, and Joab returned to Jerusalem.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 19: War With Ammon and Syria

points: After the year expired, at the time kings go to battle, Joab led the army, wasted the country of Ammon, and besieged Rabbah while David stayed at Jerusalem.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 20: The Fall of Rabbah and the Giants

points: Joab objected, asking why the king would require this thing and be a cause of trespass to Israel, but the king's word prevailed.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 21: David Numbers Israel

points: Joab numbered the people: a thousand thousand and a hundred thousand men that drew sword in Israel, and four hundred threescore and ten thousand in Judah.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 21: David Numbers Israel

points: Joab left Levi and Benjamin uncounted because the king's word was abominable to him.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 21: David Numbers Israel
